builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: FlowGenesis: Representation-Driven Self-Organization of Neural Architectures
summary: The method replaces fixed pre-specified network widths and separate architecture search with online neuron splitting and pruning driven by Representation Flux, a statistic on minibatch mean-activation changes. It adds per-step bookkeeping of Flux statistics and function-preserving split operations, increasing training complexity and implementation risk without a demonstrated reduction in training compute or wall-clock time. Persistently noisy or unstable Flux estimates could trigger spurious splits or harmful pruning, destabilizing training or degrading accuracy, and reported results are limited to small-scale image and text classification benchmarks.
rationale: The mechanism is implementable on a single GPU, but the paper shows only comparable accuracy with no quantified efficiency gain, so adoption should follow workload-specific validation on the reader's tasks.
technique: Representation-flux-driven neuron birth and pruning during training

claims.statement: The method replaces fixed pre-specified network widths and separate architecture search with online neuron splitting and pruning driven by Representation Flux, a statistic on minibatch mean-activation changes. It adds per-step bookkeeping of Flux statistics and function-preserving split operations, increasing training complexity and implementation risk without a demonstrated reduction in training compute or wall-clock time. Persistently noisy or unstable Flux estimates could trigger spurious splits or harmful pruning, destabilizing training or degrading accuracy, and reported results are limited to small-scale image and text classification benchmarks.

In task-incremental continual learning, representation-guided structural adaptation allocates fewer neurons and parameters to successive tasks than fixed-width Progressive Neural Networks while maintaining comparable accuracy; no numeric factor is reported.
